title: A video study measures missed landmarks and conditional clinician acceptance
summary: A YOLOv7 study of 40 laparoscopic videos found test recall of 77.3% for one anatomical landmark and 88.0–91.7% for the other landmark subtypes. Both required landmarks were detected in 342 of 360 eligible test images. Three surgeons accepted an average of 95.71% of overlays only in that successfully detected subset; no surgical outcome improvement was established.

source_review.scope: Primary article full-text bibliographic metadata and relevant computational evaluation Methods/Results: sec2.2, sec2.7, sec3.1, sec3.2. Primary-source caveat and denominator review; candidate-panel identity corrected where relevant.

evidence.ai_role: YOLOv7 fitted the represented classification or candidate-selection model; preprocessing and expert reference labels are distinguished from the learned contribution.
evidence.tested: The 3,200 annotated images were split into 2,240 training, 320 validation and 640 test images. Both landmarks were present in 360 test images; the model detected both in 342, which were rated by three surgeons.
evidence.unknown: Video/patient separation between image splits is not established. Overlay acceptance excludes 18 images with missed joint detections and is an average of surgeon judgments, not a patient outcome. The live demonstration does not establish prospective comparative benefit.
